title: Sample idea: automate client onboarding
idea: Replace the onboarding calls with an automated email sequence and a self-serve setup form for every new client.

rounds.name: Opening positions
notes: Onboarding eats two weeks of account manager time per client. I'd automate the paperwork part today.
I think it should be this way: big clients still get a person. Nobody wants a form after signing a six-figure contract.
Which steps actually stall? I'd measure where clients drop off before we automate anything.
Emails alone read as cold. Each one should say who to call.
If setup time halves, revenue starts two weeks sooner. That pays for the build.
rounds.card: Automate the onboarding paperwork and setup form for every client, with a named contact in each email.
credits: a named contact in each email

rounds.name: Pushback and concessions
notes: Fair. Clients over a set contract size keep a kickoff call, everything else goes self-serve.
A form that accepts anything just moves the errors downstream. Validate data at entry.
If the sequence stalls, it must hand off to a person after three days of silence.
I'll accept starting now if we track time-to-first-value per client from day one.
Smaller clients get the robot and big ones get people? Give every client a call on request.
rounds.card: Self-serve onboarding with validated forms for most clients, a kickoff call for large accounts or on request, and a person stepping in after three quiet days.
credits: a kickoff call for large accounts
a person stepping in after three quiet days

rounds.name: Best version
notes: Pilot with next month's new clients only and compare against last quarter.
Validated intake, human fallback, clear trigger. That's a sturdy design.
Competitors sell white-glove onboarding. Keep that promise visible in the sales pitch.
rounds.card: Pilot with next month's clients: validated self-serve setup, a call for large accounts or on request, handoff after three quiet days, time-to-first-value tracked.

gates.finding: Roughly two weeks of staff time back per client.
Forms and email tools already in use.
Client data entered wrong could reach billing.
gates.change: Billing fields need a human check before first invoice.

gates.finding: Every client can still ask for a person.

gates.change: Define quiet as no form progress and no reply.

final: For next month's new clients: a validated self-serve setup form and email sequence, a kickoff call for large accounts or anyone who asks, and a person stepping in after three days with no progress or reply. Billing fields get a human check before the first invoice, and time-to-first-value is tracked against last quarter.
changed: Large accounts keep a kickoff call
Anyone can ask for a person
Human handoff after three quiet days
Billing check before the first invoice
dissent: The Strategist thinks self-serve weakens the white-glove promise and wants sales to keep selling it.
final_credits: a kickoff call for large accounts
a person stepping in after three days with no progress or reply
Billing fields get a human check before the first invoice
time-to-first-value is tracked against last quarter
